note: claude-opus-5-5、入力 2431 / 出力 2069 トークン

data.interpretation: The KPI has two parts. The main aim is to maximize town-wide deliveries that meet the promised times (120 s from order to pickup, 120 s from pickup to delivery), which maps to on_time_deliveries. The second part, 'no company's customers should be kept waiting badly', is a fairness or floor condition across companies. It can be read three ways: as a minimum per-company on-time rate (min_company_on_time_rate), as a cap on the spread between companies (on_time_rate_gap), or as avoiding very late or never-delivered orders (late_deliveries, unfinished). The promised times are taken as fixed by the contract (DELIVERY_SLA). They are part of the measurement, not something to change in order to raise the count.

options.label: Maximize town-wide on-time deliveries with a per-company floor

goals.text: Primary: number of deliveries across the town completed within the promised pickup and delivery times.
Monitor: on-time rate of the worst-served company should not decline.
Monitor: orders left undelivered at period end should not grow. This prevents gains made by abandoning hard orders.
Monitor: late deliveries should not grow.

guards.text: Every company must keep at least a 70% on-time rate. The threshold is provisional; the human should set it after seeing the baseline.

options.note: Most direct reading of the KPI. Total on-time throughput is the objective, and fairness is a hard floor on the worst company. The 0.7 floor is a placeholder because the baseline per-company rates are not yet known.

options.label: Fairness first: raise the worst company's on-time rate

goals.text: Primary: on-time rate of the worst-served company.
Monitor: town-wide on-time deliveries should not decline.
Monitor: spread of on-time rates between companies should not grow.
Monitor: undelivered orders at period end should not grow.

guards.text: No more than 3 orders may remain undelivered at period end. The threshold is provisional.

options.note: Treats the 'no company kept waiting badly' clause as the main concern. This fits if one company is currently clearly disadvantaged by the road rules, but it may accept lower total throughput.

options.label: Maximize on-time deliveries with a cap on inter-company disparity

goals.text: Monitor: gap between the best and worst company on-time rates.
Monitor: undelivered orders at period end should not grow.

guards.text: The difference between the highest and lowest company on-time rates must stay at or below 15 percentage points. The threshold is provisional.

options.note: Reads 'badly' as relative to other companies rather than as an absolute level. A gap cap can be met by making the best company worse, so it is a weaker protection for customers than option 1's floor.

concerns: 'Kept waiting badly' is ambiguous. It could mean an absolute floor on each company's on-time rate, a limit on disparity between companies, or avoiding very late or never-delivered orders. Each reading leads to a different evaluation.
Maximizing the town-wide total can conflict with fairness. Rule changes that favor the busiest company's routes may raise on_time_deliveries while one company's customers wait much longer.
on_time_deliveries alone is a proxy. It can rise while orders that are hard to serve on time are left unfinished, so unfinished and late_deliveries must be watched.
The guard thresholds (0.7 floor, 0.15 gap, 3 unfinished) are placeholders because no baseline has been measured. The human should confirm or adjust them after the first baseline run.
Raising the on-time count by relaxing the 120 s promises would be a DELIVERY_SLA contract change. It must be decided by a human and should not be counted as an improvement under this KPI.
